title: Plan batched or fused work only where it preserves logical results and boundaries

facts.note: Applies while planning wagons/WMBTs/acceptances and while implementing batching; a phase observer is needed to tell these apart.
Task text mentions batching/fusion, amortizing overhead, repeated work, or orchestration behavior.

values: repeated homogeneous operations, database queries, vectorizable computation or repeated setup
facts.note: Spotting batchable repeated work or vectorizable computation in a plan or code takes judgment; no detector exists.

fires: A plan or wagon contains repeated homogeneous calls, database queries or repeated setup that could be combined to amortize I/O, setup, serialization or scheduling overhead, even before anyone proposes batching.
A plan contains vectorizable computation that could be fused, even before anyone proposes fusion.
A plan proposes fusing vectorizable computations.
A WMBT or acceptance is being written for a batched or fused path inside a wagon, or an agent is implementing one.

A plan or request relies on orchestration or runtime behavior that is not implemented (such as batch dispatch, scheduling or retries) and justifies it by citing this pattern. The rule fires to apply the caution that such behavior cannot be inferred.
doesNotFire: Single, non-repeated operations with no overhead to amortize.
Work with no repeated homogeneous operations, queries, vectorizable computation or repeated setup.

given: a plan has repeated homogeneous operations, database queries, vectorizable computation or repeated setup
when: the planner decides whether to batch or fuse it
then: combine compatible calls or computations to amortize I/O, setup, serialization or scheduling overhead only without changing accepted logical results, preserving item identity, failure independence, transaction/authority boundaries, order and resource limits.
prefer: Keep batching internal to a wagon (the normal case); no journey or interlocking schema change is needed.
Write acceptances for mixed outcomes, batch boundaries, item-result mapping and equivalence; measure throughput and tail latency.
avoid: Fusing across wagon ownership merely to reduce calls.
Batches that lose per-item results, couple failures, cross transaction boundaries or reorder items.
Inferring unimplemented orchestration behavior from this pattern, or treating it as a new runtime dispatch option.
Treating this advisory guidance as independent enforcement; existing plan and source validators still apply.
why: Batching amortizes per-call overhead but helps only if callers keep the same per-item results and isolation.
evidence: Tests cover mixed success/failure outcomes, batch-size boundaries, item-to-result mapping, and equivalence with unbatched results.
Throughput and tail latency are measured for the batched path.
The batching normally stays internal to a wagon, with no journey or interlocking schema change. Reducing calls alone does not justify fusion across wagon ownership.
Existing plan and source validators apply.
verifier_detail: Guidance for agents, not independent enforcement or a new runtime dispatch option; existing plan and source validators apply.
Unimplemented orchestration behavior cannot be inferred from a pattern.
